sections.h2: Where do I take a deed in Wayne County?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds works from 224-226 E Walnut Street, Suite 100, in Goldsboro (ZIP 27533), phone 919-731-1449. The fax line is 919-731-1441, and the office's own web page gives 8:00 to 5:00 as general hours.

Real estate filings are taken from 8:00 to 4:45 with no appointment. Staff ask that nothing be walked in later than 4:45 p.m., so a closing that runs into the evening is better sent by wire or electronic filing.

  • Real estate filings: 8:00 to 4:45
  • Vital records and notary oaths: 8:15 to 4:45
  • Marriage licenses: 8:00 to 4:00

If a funeral home or an heir needs paperwork rather than land records, the page lists a fax number, 919-731-1441, and an email option. Land and vital records share the building, but each service has its own window hours, so call 919-731-1449 before driving over with a time sensitive filing.

sections.h2: What is kept at the Wayne County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is the custodian of county land and business records: deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions and cancellations, powers of attorney, assumed business names and separation agreements. Marriage licenses, notary commissions and DD-214 discharge recordings come from the same counter.

The archive reaches back to 1913. The online index covers most real estate papers from 1971 onward, so an older tract usually means a visit.

Funeral homes have their own routine: email registerofdeeds@waynegov.com, or drop off a request in person, and staff call when the order is ready. Wills are not accepted here. The page sends people to the Clerk of Courts at 919-722-6100.

sections.h2: Is the office only a filing counter?
sections.html:
Yes. It records what is handed over, and North Carolina law keeps its staff from practicing law. They will not draft a deed, explain a form's effect or help fill in blanks.

So most Wayne County sales run through a lawyer or title firm that prepares the deed, searches title, gathers the tax and delivers the filing.

Owners selling without an agent can still use an attorney only for the paper work. Ask whether the attorney will handle the recording, and who pays the fees.

A seller who plans to skip a lawyer should still call the office first and ask what the counter will and will not check. Staff can say whether a packet arrived in the right form to file, though they will not say whether the document does what you want.

sections.h2: Can a closing office eRecord in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Yes. Wayne County takes every document type by eRecording, and the eRecording page says plats can now be submitted this way. The office lists approved vendors that firms must choose from first.

The vendor helps the firm complete a submitter agreement. Within two business days of processing, the Register of Deeds emails an identification number, which every electronic filing needs.

  • Choose an authorized vendor
  • Complete the submitter agreement
  • Receive the ID number by email
  • Submit deeds and deeds of trust electronically

Vendors must hold approval under G.S. 47-14(a1), says the county page. Individual sellers rarely sign up, since their title company does.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Recording charges from G.S. 161-10, collected by the Wayne County office
FilingCharge
Deed or other general instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages; $4.00 for every page past that
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages; $4.00 each page after
Release of a loan (satisfaction)Free
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Certified copy$5.00 plus $2.00 a further page

The statute calls the schedule exclusive and says payment comes before filing. Phone the office for the amount due on your packet.

sections.h2: How does the seller's transfer tax work in Wayne County?
sections.html:
The seller owes the state deed excise tax, paid at the Goldsboro counter ahead of recording, at one dollar for each five hundred dollars (or part) of value conveyed (G.S. 105-228.30).

The settlement statement lists it. Check the figure against your contract, and ask about gifts or below market transfers.

sections.h2: Why record a Wayne County deed right after closing?
sections.html:
A deed left unregistered gives the buyer no shield from lien creditors or later purchasers for value (G.S. 47-18). Earlier registration wins.

A seller can help by clearing old liens beforehand. A paid off mortgage with no recorded satisfaction clouds the title, and lenders file releases at no charge.

  • Search the grantor index for open deeds of trust
  • Request a satisfaction from any lender you paid off
  • Confirm the legal description matches your own vesting deed

sections.h2: How can a Wayne County seller check the title before listing?
sections.html:
Run three checks before you sign a listing or an offer. They take little time and prevent most closing surprises.

  • Search the online index, which covers most real estate documents from 1971, for your name as grantee and grantor.
  • Look for deeds of trust with no matching satisfaction.
  • Match your own vesting deed against the parcel shown in the county's real estate search on the tax site.

For anything before 1971, go to the Goldsboro office and ask staff how the older books are indexed. Staff can show you where records are kept, though they cannot interpret them for you.

If a plat is involved, the office tells people to check with the Planning Department about plats and signatures before presenting them.

sections.h2: What should be in a Wayne County recording packet?
sections.html:
Your closing attorney normally assembles it, so the list below is a way to check their work rather than a task for you.

  • The signed and notarized deed, with a legal description that matches the prior deed
  • A check or account for the recording charge
  • The excise tax payment, collected on the seller's side
  • A deed of trust for the buyer's lender, recorded after the deed
  • Any satisfactions for loans paid at closing

Documents arriving by eRecording follow the same order, and the vendor's system carries the fee and tax figures. If something is rejected, the office phone is 919-731-1449.

sections.h2: Which other Goldsboro offices touch a Wayne County sale?
sections.html:
Three county offices matter. The Register of Deeds records the paper. The Tax Collector, at P.O. Box 1495, supplies the tax payoff. The Clerk of Courts, at 919-722-6100, holds wills for an estate sale.

If the house belongs to an estate, call the clerk and an attorney before looking for a buyer, because the right person to sign the deed depends on what the court has done. The register of deeds will record the deed once it is signed and acknowledged, but cannot tell you whether the signer has authority.

Marriage licenses and vital records are handled at the same Walnut Street counter, which sometimes helps an heir who needs a death certificate to complete an estate file. Funeral homes are served by email.

sections.h2: How do Wayne County housing numbers show up in these records?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts counts 9,996 veterans in the county, so discharge recordings and veteran relief claims are routine, see Census QuickFacts. Median gross rent was $965 for 2020-2024, which shapes what a landlord seller can expect from a rental.

Owners tend to stay put, so a Wayne County house may carry decades of deed history, and a buyer's title search reads all of it. An old loan that was never released is a common loose end.

If the owner has died, the register of deeds holds the recorded chain, and the estate's attorney works from the clerk of court for the will.

faqs.q: Until what hour are real estate filings taken in Wayne County?
faqs.a: 4:45 p.m. The office asks people not to bring recording packages after that time, and general hours are 8:00 to 5:00.

faqs.q: Will Wayne County staff draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. Staff may not practice law, so they cannot draft a deed or explain its effect. Hire an attorney or use a closing office.

faqs.q: How far back are Wayne County real estate records online?
faqs.a: Most real estate records are searchable from 1971 forward, while the archive itself goes back to 1913.

faqs.q: Is recording a loan release free in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Yes. State law sets no fee to record a satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust.

faqs.q: Which Wayne County office takes a will?
faqs.a: To the Clerk of Courts, which the Register of Deeds page lists at 919-722-6100.
